name: Swiss Cheese Vine
description: The Swiss Cheese Vine (Monstera adansonii) is a popular houseplant that is toxic to cats. All parts of the plant contain microscopic, needle-shaped crystals called insoluble calcium oxalates. These crystals are designed to be a defense mechanism for the plant. When a cat bites or chews on a leaf or stem, these sharp crystals shoot into the sensitive tissues of the cat's mouth, tongue, and throat. This causes immediate and intense pain, similar to biting into tiny shards of glass. It is a physical injury, not a chemical poisoning, and it usually stops cats from eating a large amount. Signs of exposure include intense drooling, pawing at the mouth, vocalizing in pain, and swelling of the mouth and lips. This swelling can sometimes make it difficult to swallow. If your cat chews on this plant, gently rinse its mouth with water and contact your veterinarian, especially if you notice any difficulty swallowing or breathing.
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: insoluble calcium oxalate raphides; sap also contains proteolytic enzymes
Mechanism: raphides penetrate the oral mucosa mechanically when plant cells are damaged, causing burning and swelling
Symptoms: sudden oral pain, intense drooling, pawing at mouth, difficulty swallowing, swollen tongue and lips, vomiting
All Monstera species carry the same oxalate toxicity — Swiss Cheese Vine, Swiss Cheese Plant, and Split-Leaf Philodendron are all hazardous
Rinse the mouth with water; seek vet care if swallowing is impaired

symptoms.name: Oral burning, tissue irritation, and crying out in pain
symptoms.notes: When the cat bites the plant, specialized cells forcefully eject needle-like calcium oxalate crystals directly into the cat's oral tissue, causing immediate and intense physical trauma and burning.

symptoms.name: Excessive drooling (hypersalivation) and pawing at the mouth
symptoms.notes: Drooling and pawing at the face are direct, immediate reactions to the severe irritation and pain caused by the embedded crystals.

symptoms.name: Swelling of the mouth, tongue, and throat (edema), leading to difficulty swallowing
symptoms.notes: The body's inflammatory response to the sharp crystals causes significant swelling. While this type of poisoning is rarely fatal, severe swelling in the throat (laryngeal edema) can potentially obstruct the cat's airway and cause dangerous respiratory distress.

symptoms.name: Vomiting
symptoms.notes: If the cat swallows the plant material despite the initial mouth pain, the crystals will continue to irritate the stomach and gastrointestinal tract, triggering vomiting.

symptoms.name: Anorexia or reluctance to eat
symptoms.notes: Cats will often refuse food and water because their mouth and throat are swollen and in pain4. Offering something cool, like water or a bit of yogurt, can help soothe the mouth, and rinsing the mouth with water can help remove the irritants.
